clue.text: Duet with rice-bowls ?

parts.note: names a simple piano duet that every beginner learns, and also the pair of eating sticks used with a bowl of rice

explanation.surface: A musical piece performed alongside some crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a duet played with bowls. CHOPSTICKS is a famous two-player piano piece, and chopsticks also come as a pair, used to eat from a rice bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known simple piano waltz for two players carries this name, and the eating utensils go with rice bowls.

clue.text: Here is your introduction to heterodoxy

parts.note: contracted to here's

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter, here taken from your

explanation.surface: A greeting that ushers the reader into unorthodox belief.
explanation.walkthrough: HERE'S (Here is) plus Y, the first letter of 'your'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heterodoxy is belief contrary to accepted doctrine, the same thing as a dissenting opinion condemned by the church.

clue.text: He has his letters from the office

definitions.text: He has his letters from the office

parts.words: He has his letters from the office
parts.note: letters patent are issued by the Patent Office, so the holder of an invention's rights receives his letters from that office

explanation.surface: A man collecting his post from work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mail from the workplace; the letters are letters patent and the office is the Patent Office.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone granted letters patent holds the exclusive right to an invention, issued by the patent office.

clue.text: Sixty-while the other eight have only ducks ?

definitions.text: while the other eight have only ducks
definitions.meaning: in cricket, a duck is a score of nought: if eight batsmen make nothing, only three have scored

explanation.surface: A cricket team's total of sixty when most batsmen were out for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as THREE SCORE: in cricket a duck is a score of nought, so of an eleven with eight ducks only three scored. A score is also twenty, so threescore is sixty.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so three of them total sixty; read as a phrase, it says three batsmen made runs.

clue.text: Many take a spin round a tideless sea

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many

indicators.note: the word spin is placed round the second a, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Lots of people go for a drive around an inland sea.
explanation.walkthrough: C (a hundred, many) and A, then SPIN put round the second A to give SPIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's largest inland body of salt water has no outlet to the ocean and so almost no tide.

clue.text: The measure of Eve's activity ?

definitions.meaning: the distance between thumb and little finger tips, an old unit of length
from the rhyme 'When Adam delved and Eve ...', using the old past tense of spin

explanation.surface: A question about how to gauge what the first woman got up to.
explanation.walkthrough: The old rhyme 'When Adam delved and Eve span' uses an archaic past tense of spin; the word is also a hand's width as a unit of measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand's stretch was a traditional measurement, and the old rhyme says the first woman spun thread.

clue.text: Concerning one slip up in the frame-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means concerning, about
I is the Roman numeral one
a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: A remark about a single slip in a criminal set-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole string, giving REILAPSE read upwards. 'frame-up' looks like a criminal plot but is an upright frame for training trees against a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis or lattice on which fruit trees are trained flat against a wall is an upright frame.

clue.text: ABC-shaped ?

parts.note: geometry labels the corners of a three-sided figure A, B and C, so a shape named ABC has three sides

explanation.surface: Something formed like the alphabet's opening letters.
explanation.walkthrough: In geometry a three-sided figure is labelled ABC at its corners.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure labelled ABC in geometry has three corners and three sides.

clue.text: Old Moneybags aboard ?

parts.note: describes the officer who keeps a ship's accounts and money, a holder of the purse at sea

explanation.surface: A wealthy old man taking a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Moneybags' sounds like a rich passenger; he is the ship's officer in charge of money.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer handling a ship's accounts and cash is the vessel's paymaster.

clue.text: A Roman Catholic bull without a highlight?

parts.note: the letter A followed by RC, the usual abbreviation for Roman Catholic

indicators.note: the bull of the zodiac goes without one letter a, which is dropped from it

parts.note: Taurus is the bull of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A papal bull missing its key point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' removes one letter from the zodiac bull. 'Roman Catholic bull' suggests a papal edict, which misleads; the highlight is a bright star.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest star in the northern sky, in Boötes, is a light shining high above.

clue.text: View of a girl between her parents

indicators.note: the girl stands between the two parents, so her name goes inside them

parts.note: her father and mother, Pa and Ma
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A family photo of a daughter flanked by mother and father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' places the girl inside her two parents; 'View' is the definition, not part of the family scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide unbroken view of a landscape is a sweeping vista.

clue.text: Return to the old islet

indicators.note: the words are turned back to front, so the string is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: Going back to a little island of long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: TO + YE (old 'the'), turned back by 'Return'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island, especially one in a river such as the Thames, is also spelt ait.

clue.text: The piece Sally changed in particular

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changed round into a new order

explanation.surface: A reworked piece by a woman called Sally.
explanation.walkthrough: PIECE + SALLY rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean above all, singling something out more than the rest.

clue.text: Male beast for example turns full circle with unsteady gait

parts.note: a stag is a male deer

indicators.note: the abbreviation for for example turns round, read backwards

parts.note: a ring is a complete circle

explanation.surface: A deer wheeling about as it totters.
explanation.walkthrough: STAG + GE (EG turned by 'turns') + RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tottering and reeling walks with an unsteady gait.

clue.text: Rapid growth is favoured by inexperienced legislators

parts.note: green means inexperienced, new to something
a house is a legislative chamber, such as the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Fast progress is backed by novice lawmakers.
explanation.walkthrough: GREEN + HOUSE. The surface sounds political; the definition is the glass building where plants grow quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants in a glass structure grow faster in the trapped warmth.

clue.text: Bobbish attendant ?

definitions.meaning: describes a hairstyle like a bob, cut straight and turned under at the ends
a boy who serves, as at a wedding or hotel

explanation.surface: A cheery young helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobbish' (old slang for cheerful) suggests a mood, but here it means like a bob: the pageboy cut is a bob-like hairstyle. A pageboy is also a young attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A short hairstyle turned under at the ends resembles a bob, and a young male servant is a page.

clue.text: Cheap joke heard in the gymnasium ?

indicators.note: signals that gym is used for how it sounds, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a gymnasium is a gym
a crack is a wisecrack, a joke

explanation.surface: A tacky quip overheard at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: GIM sounds like GYM, then CRACK (a joke).
explanation.definitionFit: A showy but worthless trinket is shoddy and of little value.

clue.text: The Red Leaf form of government

indicators.note: the letters are given a new form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A political system named after a red leaf, perhaps Canada's maple flag.
explanation.walkthrough: RED + LEAF rearranged. 'form of government' looks like the definition; 'form' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A federal system divides power between central and regional governments, describing a type of state.

clue.text: All but singular

parts.note: a pronoun meaning all people, which nonetheless takes a singular verb

explanation.surface: Almost unique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All but singular' reads as 'nearly unique'; it means a word for all people that is grammatically singular ('is', not 'are').
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun covers every person yet takes a singular verb.

clue.text: Pepper pot mine ? Could be

indicators.note: the letters could be arranged another way, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Is this pepper pot mine?
explanation.walkthrough: POT MINE rearranged. 'Pepper pot' looks like one item; 'Pepper' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet red capsicum is a variety of pepper.

clue.text: The finishing touch when a deed becomes a deed indeed

definitions.text: The finishing touch when a deed becomes a deed indeed

parts.words: The finishing touch when a deed becomes a deed indeed
parts.note: describes the final stage of a property sale, when the deed is signed and the act is done

explanation.surface: The last step that turns an act into a legal document.
explanation.walkthrough: In British conveyancing, the last step of a house sale, when the deed takes effect, has this name; it also means finishing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing a task, and the legal stage when a property transfer is finalised.

clue.text: A chieftain with a turn for poetry

indicators.note: the word for poetry is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: rime is an old spelling of rhyme, verse

explanation.surface: A tribal leader with a talent for verse.
explanation.walkthrough: RIME (old spelling of rhyme) turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim ruler or commander in the Middle East is an Arab chief.

clue.text: Nothing doing

parts.note: read literally, doing nothing at all

explanation.surface: A flat refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing doing' is an idiom for 'no way'; here it means literally doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inactive, ticking over without work, is doing nothing.

clue.text: One who flew past the Derby winning post?

definitions.text: One who flew past the Derby winning post

parts.words: One who flew past the Derby winning post
parts.note: a racehorse of that name won the 1946 Derby, and something that flies is up in the air

explanation.surface: A horse or plane speeding past the Derby finish.
explanation.walkthrough: A horse of this name won the 1946 Derby, Britain's premier flat race at Epsom; the word also means flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying through the air describes both the horse's racing and anything in flight.

clue.text: Beams, hearing of a wage increase

indicators.note: signals the word for a wage increase is taken as it sounds

parts.note: a pay rise, called a raise

explanation.surface: Smiling on learning about a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beams' looks like a verb (smiles); it is the noun, shafts of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Shafts of light from the sun are its beams.

clue.text: Nicer out, if mixed up inside

definitions.text: Nicer out, if mixed up inside

indicators.note: the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Feeling better outwardly though troubled within.
explanation.walkthrough: NICER + OUT rearranged; the whole clue also describes an anxious person who seems fine outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An anxious, overwrought person is troubled inside even when outwardly pleasant.

clue.text: Give the servant a bit of a black eye

indicators.note: the answer is a bit of the phrase, lying across its two words

explanation.surface: Punching the servant.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'blaCK EYe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A footman or menial attendant is a liveried servant.

clue.text: Ring out, ring in, the old on Salisbury Plain

definitions.text: Ring out, ring in, the old on Salisbury Plain

parts.words: Ring out, ring in, the old on Salisbury Plain
parts.note: echoes Tennyson's 'Ring out the old, ring in the new', but the ring is an ancient circle of standing stones on Salisbury Plain

explanation.surface: New Year bells tolling across a Wiltshire plain.
explanation.walkthrough: The words echo Tennyson's New Year lines; the ring is an ancient stone circle, a henge, on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric circle of standing stones in Wiltshire is the most famous henge.
